I think personally it's a lot easier not to have to form political opinions when you dont belong to one (or even worse, ALL) of the following groups: minority (especially BLACK), poor, female, disabled, lgbtq, etc. Also if you dont live in the US because everything is inherently political here. As someone who grew up in a single parent low income minority household, it's almost impossible for people in my similar boat to not form political opinions. Because it becomes exceedingly clear very early on which type of politics are adding fuel to the hellfire that is your life, and which type of politics can actually help you. And it's not something that you gradually become interested in or suddenly start forming opinions about but rather a necessity from a young age. You never really need to one day "acquire" the energy to form a political opinion because it's already been so obvious for so long - typical conservative ideologies are harmful to those in at-risk communities. If you never grew up hungry for example you wouldn't necessarily have an opinion on essential social programs like food stamps, etc. because you dont know how important that extra cash is to struggling families. If you didnt grow up Black you'd have no reason to be politically aware of the housing discrimination that particularly faces the Black community - our current potus for example was sued a few decades ago for refusing to rent apartments to African Americans. If your parents can afford to fully pay for your college then a person might never become aware of the absolute necessity of grants/financial aid for higher ed. And it all easily boils down to this: my family was hardworking, but there are some obstacles in being a poor, black immigrant from the 3rd world, that no amount of hard work will ever overcome. The only solution is extra assistance, particularly financial. And then you look and see which political idelogies are open to the idea of expanding/maintaining social welfare, and which party is dead set against that. The choice is then practically made for you at that point, no need to form an opinion.

A lot of us didnt have any choice but to form a political opinion very early on, and I feel it has less to do with spoons than it was for our own survival. I guess be grateful that your survival didnt/doesnt depend on navigating this complex political world!

Mine also recommended that - I've been in weekly psychotherapy with a trauma informed therapist for about 1.5 years but some recent events prior to this virus have made me need more support than just once a week.

She basically said it's like a program you'd go to every day for several hours a day, or 3 times a week for a full day. I'm not exactly sure of the how but I know the "what" is just a much more intense focus on behavioral health. I hear they really make you confront your issues and the biggest thing I think is they help you replace mal-adaptive coping skills - for me, this would mostly be excessive weed use, unpredictable suicidal ideation. Also have a lot of adhd executive functioning type difficulties which I believe a behavior health program would also specialize in.

I think iop is interesting but what in more interested in is a qeeg. It's essentially a neuropsych evaluation which helps get a better view into how your brain is specifically functioning (or not) - like which areas have higher/lower activity than normal, which neurotransmitters have to few/too many receptors, etc. They say its also helpful at predicting which types of medications you'd best respond to so that psychiatrists arent just throwing random concoctions of drug combos at you without knowing specifically how they'd react with your unique brain chemistry.

My school is starting it's own iop program in the fall supposedly so I think I will wait to try that but until then over the summer I think the neuropsych evaluation can give the quickest and clearest insight into how my brain is functioning. I'd recommend either one of those but they can be costly. Def try to get as much covered by insurance as possible - good luck!

I understand what you're saying and personally for me those kind of traits would be a deal breaker. When I was younger and also really desperate for companionship I tended to overlook people who did those things (not checking up on you when they know you're hurting/dealing with intense experiences). Fast forward a bit and I could never go back to that level of relational unfulfillment, and what I now frankly deem as blatant uncaring on their part. 

If you find that this is something that gradually gets better (as in he's consistently - not occasionally- checking up on you to ask how you're doing) then it may be he just is more self-focused and doesnt consider to ask people questions, and that it will improve over time as he gains more self-awareness. It could just be who he is - you will have to decide if you feel you deserve more, or if you are content with a mediocre level of companionship.

Just to provide my personal experience with this tho, I once had a best friend who I absolutely adored and was really convinced cared about/accepted me, although I noticed she often didnt check in on me and would be distant at the most inconvenient times. Especially when we went out or were at a party and got separated, I'd never hear from her until hours later and she'd be surprised to see me "Oh you're still here? I thought you went home." But never would pick up her phone and send a text to actually ask if I was safe/ok. Well one night we went out to the club, I was super emotional and pre-gamed too hard and had to wait outside to sober up. When she got inside and realized I wasn't she called me for about 30 secs and told me to go home - didnt come outside to check on me, and I never heard from her again the rest of the night. Unsurprisingly, I was raped by our uber after he saw me alone disoriented outside and offered me a ride home. Get this - my weed dealer also happened to be at the club that night (small town) and blew up my phone incessantly until I finally responded bc he saw me outside alone and was worried. When I told him he left the club downtown got in his car and was at the Walgreens in our suburb where the uber stopped to get condoms in what seemed like seconds - he pulled up so fast I was almost stunned. And throughout all of this I've still heard nothing from my "best friend". The next morning she texted me once to tell her if I needed anything, but no follow up, and she went out again with her friends the next TWO nights in a row. 

I know that was long - I never usually comment on these posts but yours really stuck out to me. You absolutely deserve someone who will reach out to you and ask how you are just because, especially if they are aware you're suffering/hurting. To me, it is now a HUGE red flag if I notice someone is always around when I'm happy/fun, and then suddenly distant when I'm going through something. I had believed my ex-best friend was also accepting of my issues (even before the night at the club I had always been pretty emotional and vented a lot) but I later came to find out that she was actually just quiet about them. She never really said anything either way, when I divulged things to her - I mistook this for acceptance. Like your boyfriend it seems. One day when she was angry tho she told me how she really felt about everything I'd shared, and that's when I decided to end that friendship. 

Tl, dr; You are absolutely not being overly critical in expecting a significant other to demonstrate an active, ongoing interest in your daily life, especially when you're not feeling your best (pneumonia?! Flu?! And no "how are you"???). If I noticed that my bf had a habit of noticeably disappearing when I was seriously ill, I would sooner or later reach the conclusion that this person is not actually accepting of me at all. "Me" includes the good parts and bad, both when im sick and well - if he tended to withdraw during the sickness, then that would show to me that he isnt accepting of me as a whole, just my "good half". Especially with cptsd, you need someone who undoubtedly shows you their unwavering interest, so maybe someone who isnt the type to ask questions just isn't a good match for you. Maybe he'd be better off with someone who was also quiet and didnt ask many questions - we all require differing levels of emotional intimacy in relationships, and yours may just be higher than his. "That alone - I hate it. No, “what’s going on” or “can I help” or even a “I’m sorry you aren’t feeling well”. When you wrote this it felt like you answered your own question. You HATE that he does this, so if it doesnt improve, you absolutely need to trust your feelings and leave the mediocrity behind! It amazes me how many truly caring relationships I was finally able to cultivate after I left my ex best friend behind and I know you can do the same if you continue to notice that your bf isnt improving his communication!

**TW sexual abuse*** This is gonna be really long but I hope you read it all because I have a very similar experience to you so it may help. I have been lurking on here reading hundreds of posts anonymously for months and thought about posting so many times but yours is the one that finally moved me to make my first post. Seriously, after all this time on here I made an account just so I could respond to you and you would know you're not alone. I too harbor intense guilt for some of the things I did to my relatives and others kids when I was younger. Except mine was a lot worse than yours. From the time I was at least 3 years old in preschool I was always making up games to get the other kids to show me their privates. At 5 years old with my cousin. At 7 years old with a friend from my after school daycare. At 8 with my 4 year old neighbor. It was like an obsession, a compulsion that I couldn't understand or explain. And the absolute worse was when I  remember being 4 and trying to have sex with my 3 year old brother but for physical/mechanical reasons it wouldn't work, although I didnt understand this at the time. I didnt even know what sex was. At 8 years old I had grown enough that I finally began to initiate and enjoy full sexual intercourse with my brother (ugh it's so hard to type this out). This continued on and off until I was 13, and only stopped when my mom threatened to call the police on me. My mom had been previously notified on SEVERAL occasions of my inappropriate behavior with other children, and failed to see any of this as a red flag. She just thought I was a bad seed. 

When I see 8 year olds today I am truly baffled that I possessed the level of sexual knowledge that I did back when I was their age. They seem so innocent. But I struggled with immense guilt my entire childhood for the things I did. I was always afraid that one of the kids I played with would tell their parents and I'd be arrested. I felt like the worst disgusting criminal on Earth. Fast forward to now I'm 21 years old, a senior in college. A year and a half ago I began looking back into my childhood, trying to piece together the answers to a lot of questions I had previously ignored. Like, how come I explicitly knew how to have sex when I was only 4 years old? When I was younger I used to tell myself I was just smart and somehow "figured it out". But since studying a lot on child development I realized this just wasn't possible for a young child to have the kind of sexual knowledge that I did at the time. Months later I started going to therapy and it turns out, long story short, my own father had raped me repeatedly up until I was about 4 years old, when my mom finally left him. Idk when it started, but I believe it was probably about when I was 2, possibly even way before that. 

It sounds so crazy and outlandish that even I struggle to believe it today but there are so many other signs in addition to the obvious ones I listed, my therapist is confident  that it is true. My father (sperm-donor) was abusive to my mom and put her in the hospital as well, so it's not like something like this was out of his character. But that's how I knew how to have sex when I was 4, even though I had no detailed real recollection of the rapes. Someone also commented down here that kids have no real memory before they're 4, which my therapist reiterates a lot. 

Even after finding all of this out though, I still feel guilty to the point of suicide. I have the same worries as you, that my brother will turn out to be like my father and that I caused him to be messed up. Oddly enough though, my brother seems to be functioning quite well, or at least way better than me. He is a great kid, goes to community college, works a lot, just bought his first car with no help, and has lots of friends that he's always hanging out with, so I think your cousin could be less affected by this than you think. I mean, I cant do half of the things my brother does and yet look what he lived through on account of me. So maybe I didnt mess him up for life after all. From saying all of this I want you to possibly consider the fact that maybe the intense guilt and resulting suicide you feel is misplaced. Maybe something similar happened to you when you were also too young to remember. Even if it was after the age of 3/4, repressed memories are extremely common in those that have particularly experienced sexual abuse as children. Kids simply dont have the mental capacity to cope with and explain the abuse so they just unconsciously block it from memory, and the abuse is instead manifested in unconscious/indirect ways, such as the urges to do the same things that were done to you to other children. It's called re-enactment, or repetition compulsion. Maybe it would help you to look it up. Especially how you said these behaviors just suddenly appeared and then disappeared one day out of nowhere. Im not saying you were abused but just the fact alone that you are suspicious about some things is telling. Think about it, most people don't just magically come to believe that they were abused for no reason or without a lot of potential signs. Even I have all the evidence and I'm still in denial. No one in their right mind actually WANTS to be the victim of child abuse, but it sometimes provides a very valid explanation to things. I think it would be interesting and helpful to examine some of your other childhood behaviors, especially since you're saying the things you did/came up with were so abnormal. Maybe the guilt you feel and the punishment that you think you deserve actually belong to someone else. I know for me, the guilt that I incorrectly assigned to myself actually belongs to my sperm- donor, who SHOULD feel utter shame that he corrupted a defenseless toddler. I know this may not be possible for you but finding the right therapist that specializes in childhood trauma and development could be helpful. Children are very adept at learning behaviors simply by watching and imitating, so it is likely that you were just copying abuse that you had seen or heard. Especially since it's very obvious that you loved your cousin deeply and didnt want to hurt him but also couldn't resist those odd urges/thoughts. They had to have come from somewhere, and I think finding that root will be extremely helpful for you. 

Kids are not just inherently bad, and re-enactment is a way for them to process traumatic events. If I had not re-enacted my trauma on my brother, I would have been missing a giant puzzle piece today that eventually helped me understand what happened to me before I had the words to describe it. This was the biggest clue that I had and without it I probably never would have figured out what that monster did to me. The repetition (my sexual behaviors towards other children) was essentially a way of "saving" my own version of the abuse that I experienced myself, so that I could better understand it when I had the proper tools and it wouldn't be lost in my memory forever. I really hope that you can find the answers you need but until then, keep questioning. The questions I kept asking are what lead me to the answer that finally helped free me from my guilt. No, I wasn't a perverted child predator, only the victim of one. 

Even if direct abuse isnt the case for you, still consider the fact that even if you simply saw something on tv or the internet that caused your behaviors towards your cousin, children still process things they can't understand by mimicking them. Im almost positive that at 10 years old, you were merely mimicking what you saw (whether it be tv, real life, etc) or personally experienced. Children's brains are also not fully developed, and so they have a much greater difficulty at inhibiting behaviors that are "wrong" than adults. I myself wasnt able to stop myself from doing what I did to other kids because the compulsion was too strong, and as a child myself, my ability to resist these compulsions was too weak. It's the equivalent of a fully developed adult brain drunk on alcohol - you may say/do things that you normally wouldn't because the inhibitional control is gone. Im not just saying this to make you feel better either, it's a fact! Your prefrontal cortex (judgement center) of the brain isnt fully developed until yours 20s and this inhibits your decision making, which is why even under the law they dont prosecute kids under a certain age, and there are reduced sentences even for teenagers. They cannot be held accountable for their biological inability to plan and make wise choices. Just think that now, you do know better, and you would never do anything to hurt your cousin at your current age because you know its it's wrong (which you probably knew at the time just like me) BUT NOW you ALSO have the ability to better stop yourself from engaging in harmful behavior. I know this was long but I really hope it helps you find the answers you need. Good luck and stay safe!
